title: Chapati (Kenyan layered flatbread)

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, plus more for rolling and cooking

steps: Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl, add 2 tablespoons of oil and rub it in.
Gradually add the warm water and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each into a thin circle, brush with oil and roll it up into a rope.
Coil each rope into a snail shape, tuck the end underneath and let rest for 10 minutes. Roll each coil out again into a round about 20 cm wide.
Cook on a hot dry pan for about 1 minute until it begins to bubble, then flip, brush with oil and cook for another minute or two until golden spots appear on both sides.
Stack the chapatis in a clean cloth to keep them soft and serve warm with stew or beans.

title: Kachumbari (Kenyan fresh tomato and onion salad)

ingredients.name: hot green chilli, finely chopped (or 1/2 scotch bonnet)

steps: Soak the sliced onion in cold salted water for 10 minutes, then drain well. This softens its sharpness.
Combine the tomatoes, drained onion, chilli and coriander in a bowl.
Add the lime juice and salt, toss gently and taste for seasoning.
Leave for 10 minutes so the flavours meld, then serve cold with nyama choma, pilau, ugali or any grilled meat.

title: Pilau (Kenyan coastal spiced rice with beef and potatoes)

ingredients.name: beef stewing meat, in small cubes
potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Toast the cumin seeds, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute, then crush them roughly. This is your pilau masala.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions slowly for 15 to 20 minutes until deep brown, since this gives the rice its colour.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices and fry for a minute, then add the beef and brown it. Stir in the tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the salt, cover and simmer for 40 to 50 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and the rice, bring back to a boil, then reduce the heat to the lowest setting.
Cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid. Rest for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with kachumbari.
